messages.content: "John is working on a project where he needs to calculate the area of two right-angled triangles. The first triangle has a base of 12 meters and a height of 15 meters. The second triangle has a base of 18 meters and a height of 24 meters. He wants to know the total area of these two triangles in square meters. Can you help him calculate this?"

function.name: calculate_area
function.description: Calculate the area of a right-angled triangle given the lengths of its base and height. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

base.description: The length of the base of the right-angled triangle.

height.description: The height of the right-angled triangle.

unit.description: The unit of measure used. Defaults to cm.

message.content:
Sure!  
- Area of the first triangle: \( \frac{1}{2} \times 12 \text{ m} \times 15 \text{ m} = 90 \text{ m}^2 \)  
- Area of the second triangle: \( \frac{1}{2} \times 18 \text{ m} \times 24 \text{ m} = 216 \text{ m}^2 \)  

Adding them together gives a total area of **306 m²**.
message.reasoning: We need to calculate area of two triangles. The user wants total area. We can compute manually: area1=0.5*12*15=90; area2=0.5*18*24=216; total=306. Provide answer.
